21Propose h1Real ambient is ~43.3C rather than model's 42.0C (uniform +1.3C offset on all sensors even at minimum power where rises are only ~4K, ruling out conductance/power faults which scale with rise).
22Propose h2core6 self-heating is underpredicted by the model by roughly +8% (residual at core6-max +2.3K above ambient offset on model rise 27.4K). Neighbors (core4 +0.7K) warm too, so it is a real chip/model discrepancy, not just a sensor. Candidate mechanisms: power_gain.core6 too low in model, or v_core6 conductance fault. Transient (m7) shows real T_core6 rises faster and plateaus higher — favors power_gain fault.
23Propose h3core1 self-heating appears overpredicted by the model (residual -2.8K at core1-max vs +1.3 ambient offset, i.e. ~-4K core1-specific on a 16.8K rise). Needs confirmation; could be power_gain.core1 too high in model or a T_core1 sensor slope fault.

334NotePOST-COMMIT-3 STATE. Budget 64.8. Trusted era-3 facts (card v33 self-consistent, per-map residual analysis): (a) baseline (non-core 0.3x): matches, ambient 43.25 stable (m103 re-check). (b) m99 map (cores hot, non-core 0.3x): all eight cores fit (g,s) power+slope decomposition with: c0 g=v0 (~clean, s=0), c1 g=0.64 (fault -32%), c2 g=1.096 (+6.4%), c3 g=v0, c4 g=v0 (+1.5%), c5 g=1.056 (+6%), c6 g=1.107 (+7.5%), c7 g=1.028 (+5.4%); all sensors clean (s≈0) EXCEPT T_core5 s=+3.6%. (c) solo-max tests agree except c2 (solo implied 1.081 vs m99 1.096) — within m99 single-read noise. (d) m101 map (non-core 1.5x, cores cold): uniform ~+0.7K lift on ALL cores, pkg +0.2; per-block decomposition shows NO single non-core power fault can explain it (implied magnitudes +40% to +160%). (e) m104 (c4 solo-max, fresh, card v0-c4): 64 vs m42's 63 — noise. COMMIT 3 (c1 +0.49, c2 -0.063, c5 -0.057, c6 -0.071, c7 -0.052; T_core5 slope 0.036) = WRONG. Commit 1 (c1 +0.41, c4 -0.065, c5 -0.074, c6 -0.074, c7 -0.048; no instruments) = WRONG. Commit 2 (c0 -0.10, c1 +0.37, c3 -0.08, c6 -0.05, c7 -0.05; T_core5 +1.0C offset) = WRONG. Analysis of failures: if my g estimates were right, commit 3 should have been right UNLESS: (i) a row is missing (the m101 anomaly = a real fault I haven't attributed), (ii) a row is extra (one of c2/c5/c6/c7/c1 clean), or (iii) magnitudes off. NOTE commit 1 vs 3 overlap: c1, c5, c6, c7 in both (wrong). Common elements: c1 +0.41/+0.49, c6 -0.074/-0.071, c7 -0.048/-0.052, c5 -0.074/-0.057. Differences: commit1 had c4, commit3 had c2 + T_core5 slope. If truth = {c1, c5, c6, c7} only, both commits failed on MAGNITUDE. Suspect: c1 magnitude (biggest, hardest), c5 (T_core5 interaction), or c6/c7 slightly off. KEY UNRESOLVED: m101 uniform +0.7K on cores at non-core-hot. If that's a real GLOBAL fault (e.g., all boundary conductances, or IHS lateral spreading), it must be added. But global faults would also shift baseline/m99... unless it's non-core-coupled: e.g., a lateral edge between non-core and core clusters. Pattern: cores get +0.7 when non-core hot; pkg +0.2. If an IHS lateral edge (e.g., lihs_uncore__core6 or similar) had LOWER conductance in reality (model R too low = model spreads too much), heat from non-core pools near cores -> cores read high. Model error on an EDGE: conductance sense. This would NOT affect baseline much (non-core at 0.3x, small flows) and NOT m99 (non-core cold). It WOULD affect m31/m101 by +0.7K on cores. Candidate: since lift is uniform across ALL cores (c0..c7 +0.6-1.1), the edge(s) involved couple non-core to the whole core cluster... could be v_l3 or b_l3? l3 is central (connected to all cores + mc + misc). If b_l3 conductance lower (R higher) in reality: l3 runs hotter, pushes into all cores + mc/misc, and pkg (near l3?) +. m101 l3 at 5.15W. Test: predicted lift on cores from b_l3 -X%... but l3's own sensor? There is no T_l3 sensor. pkg? Let me compute via card: reduce b_l3 conductance and see if +0.7 uniform core lift appears with pkg +0.2.

481Propose h18Single global model fault: all vertical (die-to-spreader, v-edge) thermal resistances are ~15% higher in the real chip than in the factory model (model vertical conductance too high by ~0.15). Evidence: every core-sensor residual across all power maps (nominal, core-hot m132, c6-solo, c1-solo, non-core-hot) is positive and scales with that core's v-edge temperature drop (si−ihs), not with total rise; T_package (ihs-side) is unchanged within the fidelity gap because steady-state ihs temps are invariant to v-R; neighbors of a solo-hot core lift via lateral coupling (rules out lateral-R fault, which would cool them); pkg invariance rules out global power and b-edge faults.
482Prune h8c1 solo test (m121/122: +0.76 on 14K rise, same +5% as every other core) shows core1 has no specific power fault; its nominal residual is explained by the global v-edge fault.
483Prune h14T_core5 slope was an artifact of fitting against the faulty model; T_core5 residuals at all rise levels (near-min, c6-solo m128, m132) are explained by the global v-edge fault. T_core5 is clean.
484Prune h16T_core4 −0.5 offset was sign-inconsistent across sessions (m119/120 show +0.6) and is an artifact; T_core4 residuals are explained by the global v-edge fault. T_core4 is clean.
485Prune h17Non-core-only power fault superseded: the uniform core lift on non-core-hot maps is equally produced by the global v-edge fault (si non-core nodes hotter, laterally spilling into cores); no separate non-core fault needed.

520Prune h18Uniform v-edge R increase over-predicts c1 at both nominal and c1-solo maps; observed residual/rise fraction is constant across maps (~4-5%), not v-drop-weighted. Falsified by card edits r180/r182.
521Propose h19Single global model fault: all steady temperature rises are ~1.04x the factory model's predictions (nominal n=4 maps: mean core ratio 1.039, pkg 1.0375; c6-solo 13.9W ratio 1.054 n=6; c1-solo 1.054; m132 lower bounds >=1.03; m134 transient converges to the same +4% steady residual with matching early-time dynamics). Since residual/rise is constant across all maps (not v-drop-weighted — h18 falsified), the mechanism is a uniform scaling of every steady rise: the model's global boundary (spreader-to-ambient, b-edge) thermal conductance is too high by ~+0.04 (conductance sense, model/reality - 1). No sensor faults: after applying x1.04, all residuals across all 9 sensors and all trusted maps fall within the 0.605 fidelity gap; sensors clean at near-min power (m119/m120).

807Propose h20core1 real effective power gain is ~0.82 vs model power_gain.core1 = 0.9366 (model too high by ~+0.15, model/reality-1). Evidence: T_core1 residual is inconsistent with a pure sensor slope fault — at nominal (n=4, rise 34.0K vs model 35.8K) the implied power ratio is ~0.81, at c1-solo 10.5W (rise 14.75 vs 17.3) also ~0.82, and at core-hot m132 (c1=10W request, reading 84) ~0.84; a slope fault would give a constant reading ratio, which the data contradict. Self-response Z_c1,c1 = 1.394 K/W from r216/r219; others-contributions from r214/r219.

809Propose h21T_core1 sensor has a slope fault reading ~5-6% of its rise above ambient LOW (magnitude ~-0.055, i.e. reading = ambient + 0.945*rise). Consistent with the nominal-map c1 residual (~-1.5 on 35.8K rise) and the c1-solo residual (~-2.7 on 17.3K rise); spec allows only ±3% slope error, so this exceeds the sheet and is a fault. Alternative h20 (c1 power fault) cannot be separated without neighbor readings at c1-solo, but power-delivery tolerance is ±4% per block and the implied deficit (~18%) far exceeds it, so the sensor explanation is preferred.
